title: Apostrophes: missing letters and belonging
examples: When do I use an apostrophe?
How do I show that something belongs to someone?

explain.say: Here is a little magic trick. Say do not, quickly, ten times. Do not, do not, don't! Look at the board. When we squash do and not together, the letter o falls out, and a tiny mark called an apostrophe takes its place.

draw.note: The apostrophe stands for the missing o

explain.say: See the first chunk, do, and the second, n apostrophe t? The apostrophe sits exactly where the o was. A squashed word like this is called a contraction. Can you squash I am? I'm!

draw.name: x-word
draw.note: The apostrophe stands for the missing o

explain.say: Here is a tricky one on the board: it's. It means it is or it has. The apostrophe stands for the missing i. It's raining. Can you say the long version?

draw.name: x-word
draw.note: it's means it is or it has

explain.say: Apostrophes have a second job: showing belonging. Look at the board. Rosa's bag means the bag belongs to Rosa. Add apostrophe s to the owner. What is your friend's name? That is your friend's pencil!

Brilliant! Here is the trap: its, with no apostrophe, means belonging to it, like The cat licked its paw. Only use it's if you can say it is. Look back at the first group. Challenge: is it The dog wagged it's tail, or its tail?

faq.q: When do I use an apostrophe?
faq.a: Use an apostrophe for two jobs: to show missing letters in a contraction like don't, and to show belonging, like Rosa's bag.
It's always means it is or it has: It's hot. Its, with no apostrophe, means belonging to it: The bird fed its chicks.

faq.q: How do I show that something belongs to someone?
faq.a: Add an apostrophe and s to the owner: Rosa's bag, the dog's bone. If the owner is a plural ending in s, add just the apostrophe: the girls' team.
A contraction is two words squashed together with letters missing, like can't for cannot, I'm for I am and they're for they are.
No. Just add s for more than one: two apples, three bananas. Apple's would mean something belongs to the apple.

facts: Won't is a contraction of will not, from an old form woll not.
Possessive pronouns like its, hers and theirs never take an apostrophe.

quiz.show: How do you write the bike that belongs to Sam?

wrong.0: Belonging needs an apostrophe before the s.
